experimental_design.paired_sampling: Common random numbers: the uniform draw depends only on the case reference, so every variant faces identical luck on the same case and a difference is attributable to the rule.

variants.question: What the system ships with today.
variants.note: 3 attempts, 2 contacts, economic floor, approval threshold.

variants.question: What does a third customer contact buy?
variants.note: The most commonly requested loosening in dunning systems.
variants.verdict: REJECT: 141 governed-policy violations. Any revenue gain here is not ours to take.

variants.question: What does a fourth retry attempt buy?
variants.note: Card networks penalise excessive retries on hard declines.
variants.verdict: ADOPT: more revenue on no extra customer contact.

variants.question: Is chasing low-value cases worth the contact?
variants.note: Tests whether the floor protects margin or just forfeits revenue.
variants.verdict: REJECT: 1 governed-policy violations. Any revenue gain here is not ours to take.

variants.question: Does a larger discount ceiling recover more net revenue?
variants.note: Discount is a real cost: recovered revenue is net of it.
variants.verdict: ADOPT: more revenue on no extra customer contact.

variants.question: What is the price of the consent rule?
variants.note: Included to price consent, not to offer it as an option. Contacting an opted-out customer is a compliance breach; the violation count is the point of the row.
variants.verdict: ADOPT: more revenue on no extra customer contact.

disclaimer: Seeded synthetic simulation. This prices each governed constraint so the bound is a deliberate trade rather than an article of faith. It is not a production forecast.
